Annotate regions with a segmented signal track

Source: R/group_compare.R
annotate_track_segments.Rd

Averages a signal track over genome tiles, segments the tile means with DNAcopy (circular binary segmentation after outlier smoothing) and writes each region's segment mean and a two-class label (segment mean > 0 or not) back to df. Typical use: A/B compartment or early/late labels from an eigenvector or log-ratio track.

Usage

annotate_track_segments(
  track_gr,
  df,
  value_col,
  label_col,
  labels,
  align_tiles,
  tilewidth = 1e+05,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

track_gr

GRanges with a numeric score column and seqlengths.

df

data.frame with a region_id column (chr:start-end).

value_col, label_col

Names of the columns to write.

labels

Two labels: for segment mean > 0 and otherwise.

align_tiles

TRUE: tiles without signal get NA; FALSE: every tile must have signal.

tilewidth

Tile width in bp.

verbose

Let DNAcopy::segment() print its progress.

Value

df with value_col and label_col added (NA for regions overlapping no segment; when a region overlaps several segments the last one wins).

Details

DNAcopy::segment() uses random permutations; set a seed beforehand for reproducible segments.
